children: Oil prices rose while Asian equities fell amid a deadlock in U.S.-Iran ceasefire negotiations.

However, Tuesday's oil-price gains were somewhat capped by news that Saudi Arabia restored crude shipments through a crucial route around the Strait of Hormuz, dealing a blow to Iran. The kingdom resumed oil exports via its East-West pipeline after repairing damage caused by drone strikes, The Wall Street Journal reported.

On the one hand, U.S. officials continue to describe indirect talks with Iran via Qatar and Pakistan as "positive and constructive," InTouch Capital Markets analysts said in a commentary. "On the other hand, almost every optimistic signal has been met with an immediate rebuttal," the team said. "On the Middle East, the market is trapped in a push-pull cycle with little tangible progress."
Front-month West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures were up 1.8% at $94.27 a barrel and front-month Brent crude oil futures were 1.9% higher at $107.26 a barrel, according to ICE data.

Asia-Pacific equity markets were broadly lower as the impasse in U.S.-Iran ceasefire talks diminished appetite for risk assets. Japan's Nikkei Stock Average fell 1.4%, South Korea's Kospi dropped 0.9%, and Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index declined 0.7%. Singapore's FTSE Straits Times Index shed 0.5% and Malaysia's FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI lost 0.8%. China's Shanghai Composite Index added 0.1%.

"The main theme was risk-off," Commerzbank Research analysts said. "The dominant driver of price action was the collapse of diplomatic efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz." The strait is a key waterway through which one-fifth of the world's oil is transported.

Meanwhile, Asian government bond yields were mixed after U.S. Treasury yields hit multiyear highs on Monday. The U.S. 10-year yield rose to 5.241%, the highest level since June 2007. The two-year U.S. Treasury yield reached 4.922%, its highest yield since May 2024. The 30-year Treasury yield touched 5.561% the highest yield since June 2002.

Japan's 10-year government bond yield edged 0.5 basis point higher Tuesday to 3.090%. The yield on Australia's 10-year sovereign debt was 1 basis point lower at 5.404% and the yield on New Zealand's 10-year government bonds was little changed at 5.128%.
